Update a fit to new data, or to the current version of ctsem

Source: R/ctFit.R
ctFitUpdate.Rd

Either to include different data, or because you have upgraded ctsem and the internal data structure has changed. Works on a fit from either backend.

Usage

ctFitUpdate(oldfit, data = NA, recompile = FALSE, refit = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

oldfit

fit object to be updated, from ctFit with either backend.

data

replacement long format data object. If not supplied, the data the fit was made with.

recompile

whether to force a recompile of the Stan model – safer but slower and usually unnecessary. Stan fits only.

refit

if TRUE, refits the model using the old estimates as a starting point. Only applicable for optimized fits, not sampling. If FALSE, the fit is returned with its data and model specification replaced, and its estimates and everything computed from them unchanged.

...

extra arguments to pass to ctFit

Value

updated fit object, of the same class as oldfit.

Details

The fit is rebuilt by calling ctFit again with the arguments and model it was made with, and with its own data unless data is supplied. Arguments in ... replace the fit's own.

With refit=FALSE and new data, the fit keeps its model and estimates, including its random effects when the new data have only one subject. To predict for other data without updating the fit, use ctPredict(fit, newdata = data).

Examples

newfit <- ctFitUpdate(ctstantestfit,refit=FALSE)
